key_decisions.rationale:
harness.py:683 is work = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="fsa-rules-") and :701 is say(f"harness: scratch kept at {work}") when code != 0. I ran the exact regex and filter on 'harness: scratch kept at C:\Users\John Smith\AppData\Local\Temp\fsa-rules-abc123'. It captured [C:\Users\John], the leaf was [John], and (Split-Path -Leaf $dir) -like 'fsa-rules-*' was False, so nothing is removed. In a child pwsh with TMP=C:\tmp-a and TEMP=C:\tmp-b, [IO.Path]::GetTempPath() returned C:\tmp-a\.
Fix: Match the rest of the line, e.g. '(?m)^harness: scratch kept at (.+?)\s*$'. Accept the folder when its leaf is fsa-rules-* and its parent is either GetTempPath or $env:TEMP, the folder Python uses.
(seen by find:3:1; reproduced)

health_findings.claim: When a harness run exits non-zero it keeps its scratch copy of the repo, and RuleCases is meant to remove it for cases that expected that exit. It reads the path with 'harness: scratch kept at (\S+)', so a %TEMP% path with a space (a local account such as 'C:\Users\John Smith') is cut at the space. The cut path fails the fsa-rules-* leaf test and the folder is never removed. The path must also start with .NET's GetTempPath, which reads TMP first, while Python's tempfile.mkdtemp reads TEMP first. When the two variables differ, that test fails too. Each expected-failure harness run then leaves a full repo copy in %TEMP%. C-006 to C-014 make about 11 such runs per -Case All.
